feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV with clear progression, relevant senior-level scope, and good alignment to digital communications/strategy leadership roles. Writing is polished and specific, but impact would be stronger with more quantified outcomes, and the document has some redundancy and minor style/grammar inconsistencies.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, showing increasing responsibility from coordinator to director to consultant.  
- Strong domain credibility: Drupal, analytics, governance, multimedia, and advocacy/public-sector communications are all well evidenced.  
- Generally concise, professional writing with concrete examples such as the 10,000+ page migration, 3.5M annual page views, and in-house studio buildout.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable results beyond activity descriptions: e.g., email growth, engagement improvements, traffic gains, production efficiencies, cost savings, or campaign outcomes.  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to improve structure and save space.  
- Fix minor writing/style issues: “more than 12 years experience” should be “more than 12 years of experience”; use serial commas consistently (“content operations, and enterprise web improvement” vs other lists); keep punctuation/hyphenation consistent (e.g., “organization-wide,” “member-facing,” “front-end”).
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV’s direction, but it reads slightly generic and repeats language already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening it and adding a clearer leadership/value angle would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience.”
- Lead with current positioning and scope: digital strategy, platform modernization, and communications leadership for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Replace broad phrases like “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs” with a more concise, executive-level framing.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading cross-channel content, web, email, social, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in digital strategy, platform modernization, and the workflows, governance, and systems that enable effective large-scale communications. Strong background in advocacy messaging, stakeholder alignment, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows and systems” closely overlap with Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Mission-driven organizations” is useful here, but avoid repeating similar phrasing elsewhere in the profile/header.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this section is too broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value strategic capabilities will make it sharper.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with more senior, specific language: “Multi-channel communications leadership” instead of “Multi-channel communication”; “Web platform governance & CMS administration” instead of “Web & CMS administration.”
- Reorder for relevance and recency: lead with strategy, governance, platforms, analytics, then content/multimedia.
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout for cleaner style and consistency.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital strategy & transformation • Multi-channel communications leadership • Web platform governance & CMS administration • Editorial workflow & content operations • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Workflow automation & systems architecture • Cross-functional stakeholder coordination • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with the header summary and Topline Skills; consider shortening this section or using it only for broad themes not listed elsewhere.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” also repeats Soft Skills almost verbatim.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a broad responsibility list and overlaps heavily with earlier NACo entries and the Recent Projects section. Make it sharper by emphasizing consultant-level scope, recent strategic impact, and only the work not already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a tighter summary line: “Advise NACo on enterprise web strategy, digital governance, and campaign platform development for member-facing communications.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 impact-focused bullets; e.g., combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one consulting outcomes bullet.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/campaigns launched, users supported, workflow improvements, search accuracy gains, reduced publishing time, or stakeholder teams served.
- Use consultant verbs and scope: “advised,” “designed,” “implemented,” “launched,” “optimized,” “led,” rather than repeating “develop/develop.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Drupal microsites,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “governance/workflows” repeat prior NACo roles; keep this entry focused on new consulting-phase initiatives.
- AI-enabled search and campaign microsite work may duplicate the Recent Projects section; reference outcomes here, not build details.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes, team/operational leadership, and the most distinctive achievements without repeating themes covered in the consultant and prior NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget, leading platform modernization and multi-channel communications operations.”
- Strengthen outcomes: add results for the Drupal migration/redesign beyond scale if possible (e.g., improved publishing efficiency, performance, engagement, or reduced vendor reliance/cost).
- Make channel leadership more specific: replace “reaching tens of thousands” / “serving thousands” with subscriber, engagement, growth, or campaign performance metrics if available.
- Combine governance/analytics bullets for concision: “Built enterprise reporting across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery while formalizing publishing standards and cross-department workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Video leadership overlaps with the Associate Communications Director and footer project entries; keep the studio build here, not recurring video production.
- Governance/workflow language overlaps with the current consultant role; frame this entry as implementation at enterprise scale.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the roles before and after it. Make it more specific to what changed under your ownership at this level, with tighter phrasing and clearer outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, improving editorial coordination and advocacy delivery.”
- Tighten bullets to distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Reframe video bullet around growth/launch impact: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine workflow/editorial bullets: “Built stronger cross-team editorial planning and standardized publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” is very close to the Director of Digital Media entry; avoid repeating channel lists in the same way.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the program, not starting it.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from software inventory to capability-led phrasing; lead with Drupal and modernization since they are most supported by recent roles.

Suggested edit

- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation

items.aiFeedback:

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End & Technical Implementation
- Reorder by relevance/recency: JavaScript • HTML/CSS • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions • jQuery
- Tighten phrasing: replace “HTML5 • CSS3” with “HTML/CSS”; move older tech like jQuery to the end or remove if no longer central
- If space allows, add light context instead of pure listing: “JavaScript, HTML/CSS, API integrations, GTM, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; consider keeping detail here and trimming the Topline version.
- “Technical Implementation” may also overlap with recent work bullets mentioning CMS development and front-end implementation.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize systems actually tied to recent leadership work.

Suggested edit:
- Split into function-based phrasing to show intent, e.g. “Workflow automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier.”
- Move project-management/chat tools to a secondary label so they don’t dilute the stronger automation signal: “Collaboration & delivery: Jira, Asana, Slack, Teams.”
- Cut older/generic tools unless actively used in recent roles; Basecamp and Trello are the easiest removals.
- If accurate, add scope in adjacent experience bullets instead of here (e.g. automated editorial intake, approvals, reporting, or cross-team coordination workflows).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same value proposition verbatim.
- Slack/Teams also function more as collaboration tools than “automation systems,” so this category title currently overstates them.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this item reads as a bare software list and misses the stronger email-program leadership shown in recent NACo roles. Make it more specific and aligned to campaign/CRM use cases.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing, CRM & Member Engagement**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If space allows, add light functional context: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (campaign automation, segmentation) • Higher Logic (member email/community engagement) • Mailchimp**
- Keep platform names only; let recent work experience carry scale and outcomes rather than repeating them here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “email newsletters,” “tens of thousands,” or channel leadership language here; that’s already covered well in the 2022–2024 and 2018–2022 roles.
- Don’t repeat generic “multi-channel communications” phrasing from the summary/core competencies.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer scope and any available volume/results.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as early-career build phase: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Add concrete outputs where possible: website refresh scope, number/frequency of livestreams or weekly videos, channel growth, email/social volume, or process improvements.
- Tighten wording and reduce abstractions: replace “high-impact digital content” with specific deliverables and ownership.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and improved day-to-day workflows across web, email, social and multimedia. Provided informal supervision and production guidance to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; distinguish this as the earlier launch/build stage.
- “strengthening workflows across web, email, social” repeats later operations language; keep this item focused on setup and hands-on production.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/media. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the second sentence more specific and concise: “Produced digital and multimedia content for member-facing communications, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading episode planning, scripting and production.”
- If accurate, add scope or outcome: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or how the podcast/content supported advocacy, member engagement, or program visibility.
- Consider removing “contributed to” in favor of stronger verbs like “produced,” “developed,” or “launched.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid broad “digital content production and multimedia materials” phrasing unless you specify a distinct format; later roles already cover video, web, email, and multimedia leadership.
- Don’t overstate team/digital leadership here, since that progression is better shown in the 2015–2024 NACo roles.
